Method of Attack: Information stealer that collects browser data and credentials along with details about the infected host
Uses WMI queries and other system tools to collect host data (CPU, GPU, OS version, RAM, IP, antivirus, installed applications)
Delivers collected data and credentials to a command and control (C2) server in a ZIP archive
Checks for restricted regions and avoids infection in Belarus, Kyrgyzstan, Kazakhstan, Moldova, Russia, and Ukraine
Detects virtual machines or sandboxes to evade analysis
Modular design with potential for expanded capabilities
Discoverer: Jérôme Segura, Senior Director of Threat Intelligence at Malwarebytes
Attack Vector: Typosquatting fake Bitwarden websites imitating legitimate bitwarden.com (e.g., bitwariden[.]com)
Malicious Bitwarden installer delivered from fake URL crazygameis[.]com
Phishing campaigns through Google ads targeting Bitwarden users
Indicators of Compromise: Malicious .NET executable inside fake Bitwarden installation package
Installer metadata falsely claiming to be Speccy from Piriform
Installer signed with invalid digital certificate listing Tim Kosse (FileZilla developer) as signer
